title: The Building Operating System (BOS): IoT Devices and Systems Aggregator
authors: K. Nakamura; T. Yashiro; J. -E. Kim; S. Asano; K. Sakamura
source: 2022 TRON Symposium (TRONSHOW)
abstract: The Building Operating System (BOS) is a platform to provide standardized Web API sets over heterogeneous vendor-specific APIs for controlling and monitoring building facilities. The jq-based parser for transforming JSON data and an API bridge mechanism provide a method for both direct and indirect access to underlying IoT devices or services, allowing existing building facility management systems to collaborate with the BOS. The BOS entrusts the third-party OpenID connect providers and the access manager of the target facility, for the API user authentication and access authorization. The BOS is implemented as microservices and deployed on a Kubernetes cluster. Through our case study of applying BOS to heterogeneous IoT devices from multiple vendors, we have confirmed that existing devices can be accessed via standardized Web API sets by direct API conversions and indirect access using the API bridge.

title: On the Effect of Building Segmentation on the Induced Voltages of Urban Distribution Systems
source: ICLP 2024; 37th International Conference on Lightning Protection
abstract: Lightning-induced voltages represent a prominent factor contributing to flashovers in medium voltage (MV) overhead distribution lines. Their magnitude is subject to significant modulation by nearby objects, which can alter or attenuate the voltage waveform across pole insulators. This study focuses on the influence of building segmentation on the induced voltage along the line, compared to the case in which a long structure representing a building is considered. Using a solver based on the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method, simulations are carried out to analyse the variations in electric field strength within the designated analysis space and the temporal evolution of the induced voltage on the line.

title: On the Convergence of an Opinion–Action Coevolution Model with Bounded Confidence
authors: C. Song; A. Fontan; R. Su; J. M. Hendrickx; V. Cvetkovic; K. H. Johansson
source: 2026 European Control Conference (ECC)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical convergence analysis for an opinion–action coevolution model that integrates the opinion updating rule of the Hegselmann-Krause model with a utility-based decision-making mechanism. The model is reformulated into an augmented state-space representation, where the state matrix induces a time-varying social interaction digraph. The convergence analysis is grounded on two existing theoretical findings that establish convergence for the Hegselmann-Krause type of models and containment control systems with multiple stationary leaders, respectively. Results indicate that, if the structure of the interaction digraph stabilizes within finite time, the model either converges to consensus, where all agents’ opinions and actions reach an identical state, or exhibits clustering, where some opinion nodes act as stationary leaders while the remaining nodes approach the convex hull formed by the leaders. Numerical simulations are then provided to validate the theoretical results.

title: Scalable Estimation of Functional Reserve in Technical Building Equipment Using Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Methods
authors: N. Ahmad; M. Kruettgen; J. Mueller
source: AUTOMATION 2026, Innovation trifft Anwendung
abstract: Technical Building Equipment (TBE), such as heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, undergoes gradual performance degradation during operation that is not yet explicitly quantified by conventional indicators. Existing prognostic methods such as Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation generally depend on run-to-failure data or specialized sensing infrastructure that is rarely available in standard building automation systems. This paper introduces Functional Reserve (FR), a normalized asset-level performance indicator that quantifies the remaining performance margin between a component's current condition and its functional failure boundary on a 0–100% scale. To enable scalable deployment across heterogeneous building portfolios, a three-stage framework is proposed that combines automated asset discovery, component-specific Health Indicator computation, and a unified FR calculation. This modular design allows new component families to be incorporated by defining only the corresponding Health Indicator template, while keeping the remaining approach unchanged. The approach is demonstrated on a district heating heat exchanger in a museum in Cologne using 26 months of operational data. The framework is designed to be generic across TBE component families and produces a continuously updated metric, enabling building operators to prioritize maintenance across heterogeneous assets based on actual remaining performance margin rather than fixed time-based intervals.

title: Automated Integration of Design and Operational Data: Semantic Matching between IFC and Building Automation Systems
authors: M. Sedigh; M. Kruettgen; J. Mueller
source: AUTOMATION 2026, Innovation trifft Anwendung
abstract: The lifecycle of a building involves multiple information models authored by different teams at different times, often without shared identifiers. As a result, establishing semantic correspondence between design-phase models such as IFC and operational-phase data such as BACnet typically requires significant manual effort by domain experts. This paper investigates whether such correspondence can be discovered automatically using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation approach. The proposed method parses IFC and BACnet objects into structured records, verbalizes them, and embeds them into a shared semantic space using a general-purpose embedding model. For each BACnet object, the five most similar IFC candidates are retrieved by cosine similarity and passed to a Large Language Model, which selects the best match or rejects the set if no plausible candidate is present. A feasibility experiment was conducted on the air handling unit of the Building Automation Laboratory at TH Köln, comprising 21 BACnet objects and a deliberately incomplete IFC model. The system produced correct decisions in 18 of the 21 cases and reliably identified all objects without an IFC counterpart, indicating that the approach is feasible and warrants evaluation on larger, more heterogeneous datasets.

title: A Bayesian Method for Very High Resolution Multi Aspect Angle Radargrammetry
source: 8th European Conference on Synthetic Aperture Radar
abstract: InSAR's capabilities have been considerably improved by advanced processing techniques such as Persistent Scatterer Interferometry (PSI) and SAR Tomography (TomoSAR). However, complicated scattering situations (e.g. layover) need to be better resolved in urban areas. This paper presents a new technique for providing the 3D point scatterer location and the resolution cell configuration, based only on the amplitude of SAR images. The implemented method is based on the principle of radargrammetry and uses Bayesian inference. As compared to PSI and TomoSAR, the method is insensitive to temporal decorrelation, atmospheric phase screen (APS) and non-linear motion of point scatterers.

title: Building core technological competence: Patent portfolio perspective
source: 2011 Proceedings of PICMET '11: Technology Management in the Energy Smart World (PICMET)
abstract: Patents are generally regarded as important indicators of a firm's technical capabilities. We can interpret a firm's technological development path by analyzing its patent portfolio, and the development path can explore the core technological competence (CTC) of the firm. The topic of building technological competence has attracted considerable attention in recent research by management scholars, but has not sparked much empirical analysis. Time and effort invested in the R&D of building CTC is huge so we can analyze a patent portfolio to explore the strategic intentions of a firm. Based on the premise of strategic controllability, rather than patent citation data, this study relied on patent family members and claiming of priority patents to examine the patent portfolio of a firm, empirically validating the development of its CTCs. A company may develop a core patent portfolio of its technological competencies by filing patent applications and claiming priority. In addition, our results facilitate the prediction of a firm's future R&D direction from its patent portfolio.

title: Multilayer education for sustainable building Retrofit with renewable resources
authors: R. Wimmer; K. Reisinger; S. Prokupek; M. Burghardt
source: World Congress on Sustainable Technologies (WCST-2012)
abstract: In Central Europe population is declining whereas the number of new buildings keeps rising. To avoid building waste and high energy demand, the existing building stock should be seen as a resource that can be utilized by retrofitting. Thermal insulation in particular reduces heating energy demand. The use of insulation materials made from renewable resources helps to reach environmental protection targets by reducing waste and CO2 emissions. The project Renew Building aims to accumulate knowledge about retrofit materials and techniques from renewable resources and transfer it further to a multilayer group of disciplines involved in the building process: planners, builders, craftsmen and building owners. The knowledge will be accessible in a database with free and unlimited access after revision according to practical requirements of the target groups. To successfully reach the goal of developing a cross disciplinary exchange and encouraging the use and acceptance of regional, renewable resources in the field of sustainable retrofitting, knowledge is spread via multiple pedagogical formats: on-site and e-learning training sessions for planners and craftsmen, lectures at Vienna University of Technology, via virtual platform, brochures, and by advising experts during the construction process of demonstration buildings.

title: Development of a demand-side marginal cost of carbon abatement curve for the emirate of abu dhabi
authors: A. Afshari; C. Nikolopoulou; M. Martin
source: 2014 International Conference and Utility Exhibition on Green Energy for Sustainable Development (ICUE)
abstract: The best way to achieve emissions' reduction in the near and mid-term is increasing the demand-side energy efficiency - this is especially true in developing countries where the potential for demand reduction is significant and achievable at relatively lower cost. An ideal candidate for the implementation of demand-side energy efficiency measures is the building sector, since it contributes to a large extent to the total amount of GHGs emitted worldwide. In the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, the relative contribution of the building sector to the total GHG emissions is even higher than the worldwide average. This is due to the lower level of industrial activity, the inefficiency of the envelope and technical systems of the existing buildings, as well as harsh climatic conditions requiring the use of energy intensive air-conditioning equipment. The air-conditioning load in buildings is the ideal target for demand-side management because it constitutes approximately 70% of the total energy consumption. Using a detailed engineering model of a typical Abu Dhabi building as specified by the Emirate's Urban Planning Council, we proceed to evaluate the energy impact of different retrofits through numerical simulation. Extrapolating the results to the whole Emirate, we present a demand-side Marginal Abatement Cost Curve (MACC). A surprising number of the abatement levers analyzed in this study exhibit a positive net present value (NPV), if the cost-reflective price of electricity is used for the life-cycle assessment.

title: Large-Scale Thermal Building Stock Model for Generating Electric Load Profiles of Heating and Cooling Systems
authors: D. Kroeger; J. Peper; C. Rehtanz
source: ETG Congress 2021
abstract: The determination of the electrical supply task is a fundamental step in energy system models. Due to increasing dependencies between the electricity and the heating and cooling sectors, an adequate representation of these is desirable. Thermal building simulation is a suitable method to consider the heating and cooling sector with higher detail than standard load profile approaches in energy system models. This paper presents an approach that relies on few input parameters and allows simple parametrization of thermal equivalent-circuits. Performance is demonstrated by applying the model to the residential building stock of Germany to derive electric load profiles of heating and cooling systems. Furthermore, the model is applied to the trade and commerce sector to derive normalized load profiles for given specific annual heating and cooling demands. Subsequently, historical climate data is incorporated to demonstrate functionality. Results show good matching with reported historical values.

title: 11 Lighting and Sustainability
source: Fundamentals of Energy Efficient Lighting and Controls
abstract: This book is a comprehensive guide to quality, energy efficient lighting design and controls for commercial and institutional spaces. The highly practical text cover topics such as light sources and light fixtures, brightness and energy use calculations, financial analysis, and auditing existing lighting systems. The introduction of LEDs and the phase out of traditional light sources, along with increasingly stringent energy codes, is leading to highly efficient lighting designs. This book places quality lighting design and consideration for the comfort of the occupants on an equal footing with energy efficiency to emphasize a holistic approach. Featuring over a hundred high quality images and illustrations, this book: • Provides an overview of lighting design considerations and the design process. • Thoroughly covers light sources and lighting fixtures with an emphasis on LEDs. • Explains the requirements found in most energy conservation codes and voluntary programs including lighting controls, daylighting, and limits on lighting system power consumption. • Discusses non-design issues such as maintenance, energy audits, and the financial analysis of retrofit vs replacement options in existing buildings.

title: BUILDING CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT GAME

abstract: A computerized project management game has been developed to assist in understanding and teaching the economic and managerial problems of urban building development. title: Fire protection in hospitals, etc. (Swedish)
source: Spri Rad
abstract: Fire protection in the health service is controlled by fire laws, fire ordinances and the rules and memoranda of the National Fire Service Committee. Total fire protection, measures and equipment designed to prevent and extinguish fires, is usually broken down into different objectives as follows. The objectives are listed in order of priority: preventing the outbreak of fire; in the event of a fire, protecting persons in danger, such as those in burning or threatened buildings, as well as fire fighting personnel; preventing the fire from spreading, both inside buildings and from burning buildings to the surroundings; extinguishing the fire. This article deals with the organizational aspects of fire protection in hospitals, etc., the allocation of responsibility, personnel instructions, etc. The article also suggests measures to be adopted in case of fire. It also deals briefly with technical fire protection planning when designing new hospital buildings, and the technical measures that may be necessary in order to achieve an acceptable level of fire protection in existing buildings. In this connection, the recommendations are based on the obligatory regulations in the Swedish Building Code, 1975. The responsible authorities should take the following measures: review of the fire protection organization in hospitals; review of the introduction and training of personnel; review of the regulations governing fire protection in hospitals; inventory of the fire load density of equipment; inventory of fire fighting and rescue equipment; inventory of the present fire protection status of existing hospitals.

title: Asbestos - health hazards in perspective. Constructional uses
source: Royal Society of Health Journal
abstract: Despite a considerable amount of literature on asbestos, its uses and its possible effect on health, there is some confusion over the acceptability or otherwise of asbestos based products. The dosage needed to produce diseases, and the question of whether on balance the benefits of asbestos product use outweigh the disadvantages of their use are discussed. Future and existing uses of asbestos are listed. Recommendations are made for asbestos use: that it would be prudent to limit the use of materials containing asbestos to those purposes for which there is no satisfactory substitute; that alternative should be sought for these purposes and to substitute them as they become available; that an assessment of the extent to which blue asbestos has been used in existing buildings should be made; and that an identification should be made of the purposes for which asbestos based materials had been used, special attention being paid to those applications involving loose asbestos. Problems involved in asbestos use include the difficulties in identifying the various types of asbestos fibers present in various constructional materials, difficulties encountered in counting very low concentrations of asbestos fibers, and whether the decision to differentiate between blue asbestos and the other types as far as health risks are concerned is justified.
